snapshot.stmt:
Under the proposed uniform second-order expansion, suppose additionally that \(\|\Delta_n\|_\infty\to0\) and
\[
2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}=O(S_n/n),
\qquad S_n=A_{J_y,J_z,n}+\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}.
\]
Then the \(n\)-dependent triangular approximation
\[
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L\left[\frac{n\{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n-B^y_{J_y,n}-B^z_{J_z,n}\}}{S_n}\right],\mathcal L\left[\frac{1}{S_n}\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\{(\xi_{e,k}+\eta_{k,n})^2-(1+\eta_{k,n}^2)\}\right]\right)\to0
\]
holds, where the spectrum is repeated twice, \(A_{J_y,J_z,n}^2=4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\), and \(\eta_{k,n}=2^{-1/2}v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt n\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}\). At equality all shifts vanish; if \(J_z\to\infty\), then \(n\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}/A_{J_y,J_z,n}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\). A centered Gaussian-chaos limit is asserted only along subsequences for which the padded ordered arrays \((\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}/A_{J_y,J_z,n})_k\) and \((\eta_{k,n})_k\) converge in \(\ell^2\). If \(D_{J_y,J_z}\log n/m=o(1)\), the population kernel may be replaced by the average observed kernel. Separately, at fixed unequal laws, if \(\widehat V_{L,n}/V_{L,n}\to_P1\), \(\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}/A_{J_y,J_z,n}\to\infty\), and the displayed bias and remainder are \(o(\sqrt{V_{L,n}/n})\), then
\[
\frac{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n}{\sqrt{\widehat V_{L,n}/n}}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Thus the triangular noncentral representation is equality-local, whereas the regular Gaussian conclusion remains valid at fixed unequal laws.

defs.def:pilot-tuning-and-studentizer: For \(d\ge1\), set \(\beta^{-1}=s_y^{-1}+ds_z^{-1}\), \(2^{\bar J_y}\asymp(n/\log n)^{\beta/(s_y(2\beta+1))}\), \(2^{\bar J_z}\asymp(n/\log n)^{\beta/(s_z(2\beta+1))}\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}=(\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\), and \(\lambda_n=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\). Let \(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\) be the sum over \(a=0,1\) of the usual sample covariance of \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})\), \(i\in I_{a,3-e}\), and set \(\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\). If \(\bar s_{a,e}=m^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})\), define \[V_{L,n}=n\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}),\qquad \widehat V_{L,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{1}{m-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\{\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})-\bar s_{a,e}\}^2.\]
defs.def:whitened-spectral-array: Form \(\Gamma_{a,J_y,J_z,n}=\operatorname{Cov}_{P_{a,n}}\{\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,1,n})\}\), \(\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{0,J_y,J_z,n}+\Gamma_{1,J_y,J_z,n}\), \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}H_{J_y,J_z,n}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}\), and \(\mathsf K_{J_y,J_z,n}=K_{J_y,J_z,n}\oplus K_{J_y,J_z,n}\). Let \((\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n},v_{k,J_y,J_z,n})\) be the eigenpairs of the one-fold matrix, set \(\eta_{k,n}=v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt{n/2}\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}\), and set \(A_{J_y,J_z,n}=\{4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\}^{1/2}\).

snapshot.stmt: For the sign-paired conditional wavelet construction and a sufficiently small fixed \(c_0\), every \(b_{n,\omega}\) has zero conditional mass after multiplication by \(\cos(2\pi y)\), \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}\ge c\), anisotropic H\"older norm at most \(L\), common marginal \(R_n(dz)=dz\), and inverse-elliptic radius at most \(\rho\). Its endpoint separation from the null equals \[\frac{\gamma_n^2M_{J_z}}{8\pi^2}\{1+o(1)\}.\] The uniform Rademacher mixture and the null product law satisfy \[\chi^2(\overline{\mathbb P}_n,\mathbb P_n^0)\le\exp\{C_{\chi}n^2\gamma_n^4M_{J_z}\}-1.\] At \(2^{J_z}\asymp n^{2/(4s_z+d)}\), the exponent is bounded and the separation is a fixed multiple of \(\min\{\rho^2,r_{n,d}(s_z)\}\). The fixed-frequency no-covariate construction is positive, normalized, H\"older, and has bounded product Hellinger distance for parameter increments of order \(n^{-1/2}\).

defs.def:model-class: \[\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}):\text{the declared sampling, common-marginal, density-bound, anisotropic-smoothness, and local-radius properties hold at indices }(n,d)\}.\]
defs.def:no-covariate-witness: For \(d=0\), set \(q_{a,t}^{0}(y)=1+(2a-1)t\cos(2\pi y)/2\); use the pairs \(t=0\) and \(t=c_0n^{-1/2}\) at equality, and \(t=t_0\) and \(t=t_0+c_0n^{-1/2}\) for a fixed sufficiently small \(t_0\ne0\).
defs.def:rademacher-family: For \(d\ge1\), set \(2^{J_z}\asymp n^{2/(4s_z+d)}\), \(b_{n,\omega}=\gamma_n\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_{J_z}}\omega_k\psi^z_{J_z,k}\), \(r_n(z)=1\), and \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}(y,z)=1+(2a-1)b_{n,\omega}(z)\cos(2\pi y)/2\). The null member has \(b_{n,\omega}=0\).

assumptions.ass:anisotropic-conditional-smoothness: Each \(q_{a,n}\) belongs to the tensor anisotropic ball \(\mathcal C^{s_y,s_z}(\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d;L)\), with the \(z\)-condition omitted when \(d=0\).
assumptions.ass:conditional-density-bounds: The conditional densities satisfy \(c\le q_{a,n}(y,z)\le C\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \((y,z)\in\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d\).

snapshot.stmt: For every \(d\ge1\) in the pilot-feasible smoothness region \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3=o(r_{n,d}(s_z))\), there are constants \(0<c_1<C_1<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants, such that \[c_1\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\le\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}\{E(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}\le C_1\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho),\] where \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}\). The observable upper bound uses \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y^*,J_z^*,n}\), or the zero estimator when \(\rho\lesssim\rho_{Q,n}\). The quadratic and zero-zone lower bounds hold on the explicit sign-paired family in the mixture-check lemma. In the zone \(\rho\gg n^{-1/2}\), extending \(q_{a,t}^{0}\) constantly in \(z\) and comparing \(t=c_0\rho\) with \(t=c_0\rho+c_0n^{-1/2}\) supplies the regular \(\rho n^{-1/2}\) lower bound. Thus, within the observable pilot-feasible region, the intrinsic quadratic elbow is \(s_z=d/4\): when \(s_z>d/4\), \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\) and \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\) delimit zero, quadratic, mixed, and regular zones; when \(s_z\le d/4\), the quadratic term prevents a positive-variance root-\(n\) rate uniformly over the class. Outside the pilot-feasible region, the explicit lower bound remains valid but this theorem does not claim the displayed observable upper rate.

defs.def:anisotropic-estimator: Partition each arm into deterministic folds \(I_{a,1}\) and \(I_{a,2}\), each of size \(m=n/2\). On pilot fold \(3-e\), let \(\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be the empirical boundary-wavelet joint-density projection through \((\bar J_y,\bar J_z)\), and set \(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z)=\frac12\sum_{a=0}^1\int_0^1\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du\). With \(T(x)=\min\{2C,\max\{c/2,x\}\}\), define \(\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)=T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z))/\int T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(v))dv\), \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)/\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)\), and \(\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z))/\int_0^1T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z))du\). The event \(\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\) is \(c/2<\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}<2C\) and \(c/2<\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}<2C\) pointwise for both arms; clipping is inactive on this event, while normalization enforces exact conditional mass. The displayed operations keep every object defined on its complement. Put \(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}=(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}+\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)})/2\) and, on the zero-outcome-mean wavelet space, \[\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}=\left[P_{J_y}\{-\partial_y(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)\partial_y)\}P_{J_y}+\lambda_n I\right]^{-1}P_{J_y}.\] Define \(\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\) entrywise by \[\widehat H_{\lambda\mu}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_\lambda(y,z)\{\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z)\}(y)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dydz.\] Let \(\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)=W_2^2(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy,\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy)\), let \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be its observable one-dimensional Kantorovich derivative in arm \(a\), and let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}=\int\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz\). The explicit first-order score is \[\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\frac12\{\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)-\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}\}+\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)-\int_0^1\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du.\] Set \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})-\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\), where \(\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\). The diagonal-free correction is \[\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\frac{1}{m(m-1)}\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{i\ne j\in I_{a,e}}(X_{a,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{a,j}^{(-e)}-\frac{2}{m^2}\sum_{i\in I_{1,e}}\sum_{j\in I_{0,e}}(X_{1,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{0,j}^{(-e)}.\] Finally, \[\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}+\sum_{a=0}^1\frac1m\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})+\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n},\qquad \widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}.\]
defs.def:conditional-minimax-rate: For \(d\ge1\), define \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}\), where \(r_{n,d}(s_z)=n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\). The zero-to-quadratic boundary is \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\), and the quadratic-to-linear boundary is \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\).

snapshot.stmt: When \(d=0\), use the no-covariate growing-outcome-resolution construction rather than setting \(d=0\) in the conditional tuning rule. Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\), \[\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}\{E(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}\asymp\mathfrak R_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\}.\] At equality under the uniform density, the full-sample bias-retaining estimator has the exact benchmark \[n\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}\Rightarrow2\int_0^1\mathbb B(t)^2dt=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{2}{\pi^2k^2}\xi_{1,k}^2,\] where \(J_y^0\to\infty\), \(2^{J_y^0}=o(n)\), and \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y^0}=o(n^{-1})\). Subtracting \(2\sum_{k\le2^{J_y^0}}(\pi^2k^2)^{-1}/n\) yields the centered chaos. Thus the outcome resolution genuinely grows, the quadratic scale is \(n^{-1}\), and \(\rho_{Q,n}=\rho_{L,n}=n^{-1/2}\). This is the two-sample specialization of the del Barrio--Gin\'e--Utzet weighted quantile-process law.

snapshot.stmt: For \(q_{0,n}(y,z)=1-b(z)\cos(2\pi y)/2\) and \(q_{1,n}(y,z)=1+b(z)\cos(2\pi y)/2\), uniformly as \(\|b\|_{\infty}\to0\), \[\theta_n=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{\mathcal Z_d}b(z)^2dR_n(z)+O(\|b\|_{\infty}^3),\qquad D\theta_n|_{q_{0,n}=q_{1,n}}=0,\qquad \frac12D^2\theta_n[h,h]=\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}h(y,z)(\mathcal G_{n,z}h(\cdot,z))(y)dydR_n(z).\] In particular, the scalar path \(q_{0,n}=1\), \(q_{1,n}=1+t b(z)\cos(2\pi y)\) has second derivative \((4\pi^2)^{-1}\int b^2dR_n\) at \(t=0\).

snapshot.stmt:
Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,ho)\), there are fixed constants \(0<c_H<C_H<\infty\) and \(0<c_\Gamma<C_\Gamma<\infty\) such that, if \(g=\sum_{(j_y,k_y,\gamma)\in\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}\psi^y_{j_y,k_y}\psi^z_\gamma\), then \[c_H\sum_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}2^{-2j_y}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}^2\le\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}g(y,z)\{\mathcal G_{n,z}g(\cdot,z)\}(y)dydR_n(z)\le C_H\sum_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}2^{-2j_y}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}^2,\] and \(c_\Gamma I\preceq\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}\preceq C_\Gamma I\). The min--max principle therefore transfers the globally ordered spectrum of the diagonal \(H_y^{-1}\) reference to \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}\): for \(2^{-2J_y}\le u\le1\) and \(1\le k\le D_{J_y,J_z}\), \[N_{J_y,J_z,n}(u)\asymp\min\{D_{J_y,J_z},2^{dJ_z}u^{-1/2}\},\qquad 
u_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\asymp\min\{1,(2^{dJ_z}/k)^2\}.\] Consequently, for \(d\ge1\), \[\|K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\asymp1,\qquad \|K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\asymp2^{dJ_z},\qquad  rac{\max_k|
u_{k,J_y,J_z,n}|}{\{\sum_k
u_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\}^{1/2}}\lesssim2^{-dJ_z/2}.\] The same quadratic-form comparison and anisotropic approximation give \( |B^y_{J_y,n}|\lesssim2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}\) and \( |B^z_{J_z,n}|\lesssim2^{-2s_zJ_z}\). When \(d=0\), the Hilbert--Schmidt norm remains bounded above and away from zero as \(J_y	o\infty\).

defs.def:anisotropic-estimator: Partition each arm into deterministic folds \(I_{a,1}\) and \(I_{a,2}\), each of size \(m=n/2\). defs.def:pilot-tuning-and-studentizer: For \(d\ge1\), set \(\beta^{-1}=s_y^{-1}+ds_z^{-1}\), \(2^{\bar J_y}\asymp(n/\log n)^{\beta/(s_y(2\beta+1))}\), \(2^{\bar J_z}\asymp(n/\log n)^{\beta/(s_z(2\beta+1))}\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}=(\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\), and \(\lambda_n=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\). Assume \(L>1\). When \(d=0\), use the no-covariate growing-outcome-resolution construction rather than setting \(d=0\) in the conditional tuning rule. Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[

\]
At equality under the uniform density, the full-sample bias-retaining estimator has the exact benchmark
\[
n\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}\Rightarrow2\int_0^1\mathbb B(t)^2dt=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{2}{\pi^2k^2}\xi_{1,k}^2,
\]
where \(J_y^0\to\infty\), \(2^{J_y^0}=o(n)\), and \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y^0}=o(n^{-1})\). Subtracting \(2\sum_{k\le2^{J_y^0}}(\pi^2k^2)^{-1}/n\) yields the centered chaos. Thus the outcome resolution genuinely grows, the quadratic scale is \(n^{-1}\), and \(\rho_{Q,n}=\rho_{L,n}=n^{-1/2}\). This is the two-sample specialization of the del Barrio--Gin\'e--Utzet weighted quantile-process law.

snapshot.stmt:
Put \(e=\beta/(2\beta+1)\), \(b=4s_z/(4s_z+d)\), and \(\kappa=2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)\).  For \(d\ge1\), uniform absorption over the declared local-radius range means
\[
\sup_{0\le\rho\le1}
\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho^\kappa\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2}
{\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-b}}=O(1).
\]
This absorption holds, with the strict exponent inequalities forced by the logarithmic pilot factor, if and only if
\[
s_z>\frac{3d}{4}
\quad\text{and}\quad
s_y>
\frac{s_z\!\left[11d+4s_z+\sqrt{(4s_z-d)(100s_z+23d)}\right]}
{2(4s_z-3d)(2s_z+d)}.
\]
Equivalently, the second condition is
\[
(4s_z-3d)(2s_z+d)s_y^2-s_z(11d+4s_z)s_y-12s_z^2>0.
\]
Consequently, throughout exactly this region the observable upper bound in \(\text{thm:conditional-minimax-frontier}\) attains the intrinsic frontier uniformly in \(0\le\rho\le1\).  Thus \(s_z=d/4\) is the intrinsic minimax elbow, whereas uniform sharpness of the present observable pilot construction begins only beyond \(s_z=3d/4\) and the displayed outcome-smoothness threshold.  Outside this region the theorem's pilot-remainder bracket remains the conclusion, and equality of its two sides is not asserted.

There is also a supplemental global estimator on the existing class when \(s_z\ge1\).  Choose an odd \(K_n\asymp\log n\), split each arm into \(K_n\) disjoint blocks of size \(N_n=\lfloor n/K_n\rfloor\), and on every block use cells of side \(N_n^{-1/(d+2)}\).  Project each covariate to its cell center; at each occupied center form the empirical conditional outcome law; optimally couple the two projected empirical covariate marginals in Euclidean distance; and integrate the squared Wasserstein distance between the paired empirical conditional outcome laws.  Let the final estimator be the median of these \(K_n\) block values.  Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\left\{E(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm{dir,med}}-\theta_n)^2\right\}^{1/2}
\lesssim n^{-1/(d+2)}(\log n)^{1+1/(d+2)}.
\]
Accordingly, for \(s_z\ge1\) the upper side of the minimax bracket may be sharpened to the minimum of \(\rho^2\), the theorem's pilot-remainder envelope, and this direct-COT envelope.  This supplemental bound neither changes the intrinsic converse nor closes the pilot-dominated bracket in general.

For the opposite-fold estimator and the declared pilot resolutions, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\max_e\left[\|\widehat r_n^{(-e)}-r_n\|_\infty+\max_a\|\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}-q_{a,n}\|_\infty\right]=O_P(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}),\qquad P\left(\bigcap_{e=1}^2\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\right)\to1.
\]
The clipping is inactive on that event, and conditional normalization is exact everywhere. Coercivity and the resolvent identity give
\[
\max_e\|\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-H_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}+\lambda_n).
\]
The plug-in, ridge, and operator contribution to the second-order expansion is \(O_P\{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho_n^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\}+o_P(1)\{\rho_n/\sqrt n+A_{J_y,J_z,n}/n\}\). Hence it is negligible relative to the displayed expansion scale whenever
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho_n^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2=o\!\left(\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}n+2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}\right).
\]
If additionally \(D_{J_y,J_z}\log n/m=o(1)\), then \(\max_e\|\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1)\) and \(\max_e\|\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1)\); this extra covariance condition is required only when the population triangular proxy is replaced by its observed spectral plug-in, not for the point estimator.

defs.def:anisotropic-estimator: Partition each arm into deterministic folds \(I_{a,1}\) and \(I_{a,2}\), each of size \(m=n/2\). On pilot fold \(3-e\), let \(\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be the empirical boundary-wavelet joint-density projection through \((\bar J_y,\bar J_z)\), and set \(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z)=\frac12\sum_{a=0}^1\int_0^1\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du\). With \(T(x)=\min\{2C,\max\{c/2,x\}\}\), define \(\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)=T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z))/\int T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(v))dv\), \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)/\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)\), and \(\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z))/\int_0^1T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z))du\). The event \(\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\) is \(c/2<\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}<2C\) and \(c/2<\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}<2C\) pointwise for both arms; clipping is inactive on this event, while normalization enforces exact conditional mass. The displayed operations keep every object defined on its complement. Put \(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}=(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}+\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)})/2\) and, on the zero-outcome-mean wavelet space, \[\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}=\left[P_{J_y}\{-\partial_y(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)\partial_y)\}P_{J_y}+\lambda_n I\right]^{-1}P_{J_y}.\] Define \(\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\) entrywise by \[\widehat H_{\lambda\mu}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_\lambda(y,z)\{\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z)\}(y)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dydz.\] Let \(\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)=W_2^2(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy,\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy)\), let \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be its observable one-dimensional Kantorovich derivative in arm \(a\), and let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}=\int\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz\). The explicit first-order score is \[\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\frac12\{\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)-\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}\}+\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)-\int_0^1\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du.\] Set \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})-\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\), where \(\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\). The diagonal-free correction is \[\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\frac{1}{m(m-1)}\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{i\ne j\in I_{a,e}}(X_{a,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{a,j}^{(-e)}-\frac{2}{m^2}\sum_{i\in I_{1,e}}\sum_{j\in I_{0,e}}(X_{1,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{0,j}^{(-e)}.\] Finally, \[\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}+\sum_{a=0}^1\frac1m\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})+\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n},\qquad \widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}.\]

The explicit first-order score is \[\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\frac12\{\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)-\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}\}+\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)-\int_0^1\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du.\] Set \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})-\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\), where \(\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\). The diagonal-free correction is \[\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\frac{1}{m(m-1)}\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{i\ne j\in I_{a,e}}(X_{a,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{a,j}^{(-e)}-\frac{2}{m^2}\sum_{i\in I_{1,e}}\sum_{j\in I_{0,e}}(X_{1,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{0,j}^{(-e)}.\] Finally, \[\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}+\sum_{a=0}^1\frac1m\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})+\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n},\qquad \widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}.\]
defs.def:anisotropic-projection: For \(d\ge1\), \(\Pi_{J_y,J_z}h=\sum_{(\lambda,\gamma)\in\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}}\langle h,\psi^y_\lambda\psi^z_\gamma\rangle_{L^2(dy\,dR_n)}\psi^y_\lambda\psi^z_\gamma\); for \(d=0\), retain only the outcome sum through \(J_y\).

assumptions.ass:wavelet-regularity: The bases \(\Psi_y\) and \(\Psi_z\) are compactly supported boundary wavelets with regularities strictly greater than \(s_y+1\) and \(s_z\), respectively.

snapshot.stmt:
Under the proposed uniform second-order expansion, suppose additionally that \(\|\Delta_n\|_\infty\to0\) and
\[
2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}=O(S_n/n),
\qquad S_n=A_{J_y,J_z,n}+\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}.
\]
Then the \(n\)-dependent triangular approximation
\[
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(\mathcal L\left[\frac{n\{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n-B^y_{J_y,n}-B^z_{J_z,n}\}}{S_n}\right],\mathcal L\left[\frac{1}{S_n}\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\{(\xi_{e,k}+\eta_{k,n})^2-(1+\eta_{k,n}^2)\}\right]\right)\to0
\]
holds, where the spectrum is repeated twice, \(A_{J_y,J_z,n}^2=4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\), and \(\eta_{k,n}=2^{-1/2}v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt n\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}\). At equality all shifts vanish; if \(J_z\to\infty\), then \(n\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}/A_{J_y,J_z,n}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\). A centered Gaussian-chaos limit is asserted only along subsequences for which the padded ordered arrays \((\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}/A_{J_y,J_z,n})_k\) and \((\eta_{k,n})_k\) converge in \(\ell^2\). If \(D_{J_y,J_z}\log n/m=o(1)\), the population kernel may be replaced by the average observed kernel. Separately, at fixed unequal laws, if \(\widehat V_{L,n}/V_{L,n}\to_P1\), \(\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}/A_{J_y,J_z,n}\to\infty\), and the displayed bias and remainder are \(o(\sqrt{V_{L,n}/n})\), then
\[
\frac{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n}{\sqrt{\widehat V_{L,n}/n}}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Thus the triangular noncentral representation is equality-local, whereas the regular Gaussian conclusion remains valid at fixed unequal laws.

snapshot.stmt:
Assume \(L>1\). For every \(d\ge1\), there are constants \(0<c_1<C_1<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants, such that
\[
c_1\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\le\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}\{E(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}
\]
\[
\le C_1\min\!\left[\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\right],
\]
where \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}\). The observable upper bound uses \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y^*,J_z^*,n}\), or the zero estimator when \(\rho\lesssim\rho_{Q,n}\). The quadratic and zero-zone lower bounds hold on the explicit sign-paired family in the mixture-check lemma. In the zone \(\rho\gg n^{-1/2}\), extending \(q_{a,t}^{0}\) constantly in \(z\) and comparing \(t=c_0\rho\) with \(t=c_0\rho+c_0n^{-1/2}\) supplies the regular \(\rho n^{-1/2}\) lower bound. The bracket is matched whenever
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3+\rho^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2
=O\{\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}.
\]
In this matching region the intrinsic quadratic elbow is \(s_z=d/4\): when \(s_z>d/4\), \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\) and \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\) delimit zero, quadratic, mixed, and regular zones; when \(s_z\le d/4\), the quadratic term prevents a positive-variance root-\(n\) rate uniformly over the class. Outside the matching region, the displayed two-sided bracket is the conclusion and its tightness is not asserted.

defs.def:anisotropic-estimator: Partition each arm into deterministic folds \(I_{a,1}\) and \(I_{a,2}\), each of size \(m=n/2\). On pilot fold \(3-e\), let \(\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be the empirical boundary-wavelet joint-density projection through \((\bar J_y,\bar J_z)\), and set \(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z)=\frac12\sum_{a=0}^1\int_0^1\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du\). With \(T(x)=\min\{2C,\max\{c/2,x\}\}\), define \(\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)=T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z))/\int T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(v))dv\), \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)/\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)\), and \(\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z))/\int_0^1T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z))du\). The event \(\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\) is \(c/2<\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}<2C\) and \(c/2<\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}<2C\) pointwise for both arms; clipping is inactive on this event, while normalization enforces exact conditional mass. The displayed operations keep every object defined on its complement. Put \(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}=(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}+\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)})/2\) and, on the zero-outcome-mean wavelet space, \[\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}=\left[P_{J_y}\{-\partial_y(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)\partial_y)\}P_{J_y}+\lambda_n I\right]^{-1}P_{J_y}.\] Define \(\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\) entrywise by \[\widehat H_{\lambda\mu}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_\lambda(y,z)\{\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z)\}(y)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dydz.\] Let \(\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)=W_2^2(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy,\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy)\), let \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be its observable one-dimensional Kantorovich derivative in arm \(a\), and let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}=\int\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz\). The explicit first-order score is \[\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\frac12\{\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)-\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}\}+\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)-\int_0^1\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du.\] Set \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})-\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\), where \(\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\). The diagonal-free correction is \[\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\frac{1}{m(m-1)}\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{i\ne j\in I_{a,e}}(X_{a,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{a,j}^{(-e)}-\frac{2}{m^2}\sum_{i\in I_{1,e}}\sum_{j\in I_{0,e}}(X_{1,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{0,j}^{(-e)}.\] Finally, \[\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}+\sum_{a=0}^1\frac1m\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})+\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n},\qquad \widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}.\]
defs.def:conditional-minimax-rate: For \(d\ge1\), define \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}\), where \(r_{n,d}(s_z)=n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\). The zero-to-quadratic boundary is \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\), and the quadratic-to-linear boundary is \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\).
defs.def:model-class: \[\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}):\text{the declared sampling, common-marginal, density-bound, anisotropic-smoothness, and local-radius properties hold at indices }(n,d)\}.\]
defs.def:no-covariate-witness: For \(d=0\), set \(q_{a,t}^{0}(y)=1+(2a-1)t\cos(2\pi y)/2\); use the pairs \(t=0\) and \(t=c_0n^{-1/2}\) at equality, and \(t=t_0\) and \(t=t_0+c_0n^{-1/2}\) for a fixed sufficiently small \(t_0\ne0\).

Let \(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\) be the sum over \(a=0,1\) of the usual sample covariance of \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})\), \(i\in I_{a,3-e}\), and set \(\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\widehat H_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\). If \(\bar s_{a,e}=m^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})\), define \[V_{L,n}=n\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}),\qquad \widehat V_{L,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{1}{m-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\{\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})-\bar s_{a,e}\}^2.\]
defs.def:rademacher-family: For \(d\ge1\), set \(2^{J_z}\asymp n^{2/(4s_z+d)}\), \(b_{n,\omega}=\gamma_n\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_{J_z}}\omega_k\psi^z_{J_z,k}\), \(r_n(z)=1\), and \(q_{a,n,\omega}^{\mathrm{lb}}(y,z)=1+(2a-1)b_{n,\omega}(z)\cos(2\pi y)/2\). The null member has \(b_{n,\omega}=0\).

assumptions.ass:holder-radius-interior: The H\"older radius satisfies \(L>1\), so the uniform density is an interior point of the declared H\"older balls.
assumptions.ass:two-arm-sampling: For every \(n\), the observations \(W_{a,1,n},\ldots,W_{a,n,n}\) are i.i.d. from \(P_{a,n}\) within each \(a\in\mathcal A\), and the two arm samples are independent.

assumptions.ass:covariate-density-bounds: For \(d\ge1\), the common marginal density satisfies \(c\le r_n(z)\le C\) for every \(z\in\mathcal Z_d\).
assumptions.ass:conditional-density-bounds: The conditional densities satisfy \(c\le q_{a,n}(y,z)\le C\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \((y,z)\in\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d\).
assumptions.ass:anisotropic-conditional-smoothness: Each \(q_{a,n}\) belongs to the tensor anisotropic ball \(\mathcal C^{s_y,s_z}(\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d;L)\), with the \(z\)-condition omitted when \(d=0\).

snapshot.stmt:
Put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\), \(e=\beta/(2\beta+1)\), \(b=4s_z/(4s_z+d)\), and \(\kappa=2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)\).  For \(d\ge1\), uniform absorption of the H\"older-valid pilot remainder over the declared local-radius range means
\[
\sup_{0\le\rho\le1}
\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{a_y\kappa}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2}
{\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-b}}=O(1).
\]
This absorption holds, with the strict exponent inequalities forced by the logarithmic pilot factor, if and only if
\[
s_z>\frac{3d}{4}
\quad\text{and}\quad
s_y>
\frac{s_z\!\left[11d+4s_z+\sqrt{(4s_z-d)(100s_z+23d)}\right]}
{2(4s_z-3d)(2s_z+d)}.
\]
Equivalently, the second condition is
\[
(4s_z-3d)(2s_z+d)s_y^2-s_z(11d+4s_z)s_y-12s_z^2>0.
\]
Consequently, throughout exactly this region the observable upper bound in \(\text{thm:conditional-minimax-frontier}\) attains the intrinsic frontier uniformly in \(0\le\rho\le1\).  Thus \(s_z=d/4\) is the intrinsic minimax elbow, whereas uniform sharpness of the present observable pilot construction begins only beyond \(s_z=3d/4\) and the displayed outcome-smoothness threshold.  Outside this region the theorem's H\"older-order pilot-remainder bracket remains the conclusion, and equality of its two sides is not asserted.

There is also a supplemental global estimator on the existing class when \(s_z\ge1\).  Choose an odd \(K_n\asymp\log n\), split each arm into \(K_n\) disjoint blocks of size \(N_n=\lfloor n/K_n\rfloor\), and on every block use cells of side \(N_n^{-1/(d+2)}\).  Project each covariate to its cell center; at each occupied center form the empirical conditional outcome law; optimally couple the two projected empirical covariate marginals in Euclidean distance; and integrate the squared Wasserstein distance between the paired empirical conditional outcome laws.  Let the final estimator be the median of these \(K_n\) block values.  Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\left\{E(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm{dir,med}}-\theta_n)^2\right\}^{1/2}
\lesssim n^{-1/(d+2)}(\log n)^{1+1/(d+2)}.
\]
Accordingly, for \(s_z\ge1\) the upper side of the minimax bracket may be sharpened to the minimum of \(\rho^2\), the theorem's pilot-remainder envelope, and this direct-COT envelope.  This supplemental bound neither changes the intrinsic converse nor closes the pilot-dominated bracket in general.

For each point-estimator outcome resolution, let \(J_y^{\mathrm{op}}\ge J_y\) be the smallest integer satisfying \(2^{-2J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\). \[

=\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}
\widehat H_{\mathrm{form},J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}

\[

\]

\[

=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}^{\top}G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}
\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)h(y,z)\,dy\,dR_n(z).

Under the uniform second-order expansion, suppose additionally that \(\|\Delta_n\|_\infty\to0\) and
\[

\qquad

\]
Then the finite-\(n\) Gaussian-quadratic proxy based on the corrected raw-moment kernel satisfies
\[
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L\left[\frac{n\{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n-B^y_{J_y,n}-B^z_{J_z,n}\}}{S_n}\right],
\mathcal L\left[\frac1{S_n}\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}
\{(\xi_{e,k}+\eta_{k,n})^2-(1+\eta_{k,n}^2)\}\right]
\right)\to0,
\]
where \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}B_{J_y,J_z,n}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}\), the spectrum is repeated twice,
\[
A_{J_y,J_z,n}^2=4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2,
\qquad
\eta_{k,n}=2^{-1/2}v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt n\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}.
\]
The same proxy and the normalized estimator are diffuse locally Gaussian:
\[
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L\left[\frac{n\{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n-B^y_{J_y,n}-B^z_{J_z,n}\}}{S_n}\right],
\mathcal N\!\left(0,\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}^2+nV_{L,n}}{S_n^2}\right)
\right)\to0.
\]
In particular, at equality all shifts and the linear projection vanish and
\[
\frac{n\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}}{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]

Separately, at fixed unequal laws, if \(\widehat V_{L,n}/V_{L,n}\to_P1\), \(\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}/A_{J_y,J_z,n}\to\infty\), and the displayed bias and remainder are \(o(\sqrt{V_{L,n}/n})\), then
\[

\]
No fixed or subsequential non-Gaussian chaos is asserted in this growing-covariate-resolution regime.

Assume \(L>1\), and put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\). For every \(d\ge1\), there are constants \(0<c_1<C_1<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants, such that
\[
c_1\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\le\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}\{E(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}
\]
\[
\le C_1\min\!\left[\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\right],
\]
where \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}\). The observable upper bound uses \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y^*,J_z^*,n}\), or the zero estimator when \(\rho\lesssim\rho_{Q,n}\). The quadratic and zero-zone lower bounds hold on the explicit sign-paired family in the mixture-check lemma. In the zone \(\rho\gg n^{-1/2}\), extending \(q_{a,t}^{0}\) constantly in \(z\) and comparing \(t=c_0\rho\) with \(t=c_0\rho+c_0n^{-1/2}\) supplies the regular \(\rho n^{-1/2}\) lower bound. The bracket is matched whenever
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2
=O\{\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}.
\]
In this matching region the intrinsic quadratic elbow is \(s_z=d/4\): when \(s_z>d/4\), \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\) and \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\) delimit zero, quadratic, mixed, and regular zones; when \(s_z\le d/4\), the quadratic term prevents a positive-variance root-\(n\) rate uniformly over the class. Outside the matching region, the displayed two-sided bracket is the conclusion and its tightness is not asserted.

defs.def:anisotropic-estimator:

\]

\[

\]
\[

\]
and the raw-moment-coordinate Hessian
\[

=\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}
\widehat H_{\mathrm{form},J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}.
\]

\[

\]

\[

\[

snapshot.stmt:
Assume \(L>1\). When \(d=0\), use the no-covariate growing-outcome-resolution construction rather than setting \(d=0\) in the conditional tuning rule. Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}\{E(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}\asymp\mathfrak R_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\}.
\]
At equality under the uniform density, the full-sample bias-retaining estimator has the exact benchmark
\[
n\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}\Rightarrow2\int_0^1\mathbb B(t)^2dt=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{2}{\pi^2k^2}\xi_{1,k}^2,
\]
where \(J_y^0\to\infty\), \(2^{J_y^0}=o(n)\), and \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y^0}=o(n^{-1})\). Subtracting \(2\sum_{k\le2^{J_y^0}}(\pi^2k^2)^{-1}/n\) yields the centered chaos. Thus the outcome resolution genuinely grows, the quadratic scale is \(n^{-1}\), and \(\rho_{Q,n}=\rho_{L,n}=n^{-1/2}\). This is the two-sample specialization of the del Barrio--Gin\'e--Utzet weighted quantile-process law.

defs.def:no-covariate-branch:
When \(d=0\), define the empirical distribution function in arm \(a\) by \(\widehat F_{a,n}(y)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{Y_{a,i,n}\le y\}\) and its left-continuous generalized inverse by \(\widehat Q_{a,n}(u)=\inf\{y\in[0,1]:\widehat F_{a,n}(y)\ge u\}\). Let \(V^Q_{J_y}\) be the span of all boundary scaling functions and wavelets from \(\Psi_y\) through level \(J_y\), with the constant scaling function retained, and let \(P^Q_{J_y}\) be the \(L^2[0,1]\)-orthogonal projector onto \(V^Q_{J_y}\). Define the full-sample statistic
\[
\widehat\theta^0_{J_y,n}=\int_0^1\left[P^Q_{J_y}\{\widehat Q_{1,n}-\widehat Q_{0,n}\}(u)\right]^2du .
\]
Choose \(J_y^0\) so that \(2^{J_y^0}\to\infty\), \(2^{J_y^0}=o(n)\), and \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y^0}=o(n^{-1})\). The square retains its diagonal term. Define \(\mathfrak R_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\}\).
defs.def:no-covariate-witness: For \(d=0\), set \(q_{a,t}^{0}(y)=1+(2a-1)t\cos(2\pi y)/2\); use the pairs \(t=0\) and \(t=c_0n^{-1/2}\) at equality, and \(t=t_0\) and \(t=t_0+c_0n^{-1/2}\) for a fixed sufficiently small \(t_0\ne0\).

snapshot.stmt:
Put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\), \(e=\beta/(2\beta+1)\), \(b=4s_z/(4s_z+d)\), and \(\kappa=2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)\).  For \(d\ge1\), uniform absorption of the H\"older-valid pilot remainder over the declared local-radius range means
\[
\sup_{0\le\rho\le1}
\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{a_y\kappa}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2}
{\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-b}}=O(1).
\]
This absorption holds, with the strict exponent inequalities forced by the logarithmic pilot factor, if and only if
\[
s_z>\frac{3d}{4}
\quad\text{and}\quad
s_y>
\frac{s_z\!\left[11d+4s_z+\sqrt{(4s_z-d)(100s_z+23d)}\right]}
{2(4s_z-3d)(2s_z+d)}.
\]
Equivalently, the second condition is
\[
(4s_z-3d)(2s_z+d)s_y^2-s_z(11d+4s_z)s_y-12s_z^2>0.
\]
Consequently, throughout exactly this region the observable upper bound in \(\text{thm:conditional-minimax-frontier}\) attains the intrinsic frontier uniformly in \(0\le\rho\le1\).  Thus \(s_z=d/4\) is the intrinsic minimax elbow, whereas uniform sharpness of the present observable pilot construction begins only beyond \(s_z=3d/4\) and the displayed outcome-smoothness threshold.  Outside this region the theorem's H\"older-order pilot-remainder bracket remains the conclusion, and equality of its two sides is not asserted.

There is also a supplemental global estimator on the existing class when \(s_z\ge1\).  Choose an odd \(K_n\asymp\log n\), split each arm into \(K_n\) disjoint blocks of size \(N_n=\lfloor n/K_n\rfloor\), and on every block use cells of side \(N_n^{-1/(d+2)}\).  Project each covariate to its cell center; at each occupied center form the empirical conditional outcome law; optimally couple the two projected empirical covariate marginals in Euclidean distance; and integrate the squared Wasserstein distance between the paired empirical conditional outcome laws.  Let the final estimator be the median of these \(K_n\) block values.  Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\left\{E(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm{dir,med}}-\theta_n)^2\right\}^{1/2}
\lesssim n^{-1/(d+2)}(\log n)^{1+1/(d+2)}.
\]
Accordingly, for \(s_z\ge1\) the upper side of the minimax bracket may be sharpened to the minimum of \(\rho^2\), the theorem's pilot-remainder envelope, and this direct-COT envelope.  This supplemental bound neither changes the intrinsic converse nor closes the pilot-dominated bracket in general.

For each point-estimator outcome resolution, let \(J_y^{\mathrm{op}}\ge J_y\) be the smallest integer satisfying \(2^{-2J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\). Let \(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\) be the sum over \(a=0,1\) of the usual sample covariance of \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})\), \(i\in I_{a,3-e}\), and set
\[
\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}.
\]
If \(\bar s_{a,e}=m^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})\), define
\[
V_{L,n}=n\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}),
\qquad
\widehat V_{L,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{1}{m-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\{\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})-\bar s_{a,e}\}^2.
\]

snapshot.stmt:
Assume \(L>1\), and put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\). For every \(d\ge1\), there are constants \(0<c_1<C_1<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants, such that
\[
c_1\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\le\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}\{E(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}
\]
\[
\le C_1\min\!\left[\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\right],
\]
where \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}\). The observable upper bound uses \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y^*,J_z^*,n}\), or the zero estimator when \(\rho\lesssim\rho_{Q,n}\). The quadratic and zero-zone lower bounds hold on the explicit sign-paired family in the mixture-check lemma. In the zone \(\rho\gg n^{-1/2}\), extending \(q_{a,t}^{0}\) constantly in \(z\) and comparing \(t=c_0\rho\) with \(t=c_0\rho+c_0n^{-1/2}\) supplies the regular \(\rho n^{-1/2}\) lower bound. The bracket is matched whenever
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2
=O\{\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}.
\]
In this matching region the intrinsic quadratic elbow is \(s_z=d/4\): when \(s_z>d/4\), \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\) and \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\) delimit zero, quadratic, mixed, and regular zones; when \(s_z\le d/4\), the quadratic term prevents a positive-variance root-\(n\) rate uniformly over the class. Outside the matching region, the displayed two-sided bracket is the conclusion and its tightness is not asserted.

defs.def:anisotropic-estimator:
Partition each arm into deterministic folds \(I_{a,1}\) and \(I_{a,2}\), each of size \(m=n/2\). On pilot fold \(3-e\), let \(\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be the empirical boundary-wavelet joint-density projection through \((\bar J_y,\bar J_z)\), and set \(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z)=\frac12\sum_{a=0}^1\int_0^1\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du\). With \(T(x)=\min\{2C,\max\{c/2,x\}\}\), define \(\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)=T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z))/\int T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(v))dv\), \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)/\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)\), and \(\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z))/\int_0^1T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z))du\). The event \(\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\) is \(c/2<\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}<2C\) and \(c/2<\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}<2C\) pointwise for both arms; clipping is inactive on this event, while normalization enforces exact conditional mass. The displayed operations keep every object defined on its complement. Put \(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}=(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}+\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)})/2\) and, on the oversampled zero-outcome-mean wavelet space through \(J_y^{\mathrm{op}}\), set
\[
\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}=
\left[P_{J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}\{-\partial_y(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)\partial_y)\}P_{J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}+\lambda_n I\right]^{-1}P_{J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)^{\top}\,dy\,\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz,
\]
\[
\widehat H_{\mathrm{form},J_y,J_z,n;\lambda\mu}^{(-e)}
=\int\Phi_\lambda(y,z)\{\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z)\}(y)\,dy\,\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz,
\]
and the raw-moment-coordinate Hessian
\[
\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
=\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}
\widehat H_{\mathrm{form},J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}.
\]
Let \(\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)=W_2^2(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy,\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy)\), let \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be its observable one-dimensional Kantorovich derivative in arm \(a\), and let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}=\int\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz\). The explicit first-order score is
\[
\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\frac12\{\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)-\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}\}+\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)-\int_0^1\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du.
\]
Set \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})-\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\), where \(\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\). The diagonal-free correction in raw moment coordinates is
\[
\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\frac{1}{m(m-1)}\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{i\ne j\in I_{a,e}}(X_{a,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{a,j}^{(-e)}-\frac{2}{m^2}\sum_{i\in I_{1,e}}\sum_{j\in I_{0,e}}(X_{1,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{0,j}^{(-e)}.
\]
Finally,
\[
\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}+\sum_{a=0}^1\frac1m\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})+\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n},
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}.
\]

snapshot.stmt:
Under the uniform second-order expansion, suppose additionally that \(\|\Delta_n\|_\infty\to0\) and
\[
2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}=O(S_n/n),
\qquad
S_n=A_{J_y,J_z,n}+\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}.
\]
Then the finite-\(n\) Gaussian-quadratic proxy based on the corrected raw-moment kernel satisfies
\[
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L\left[\frac{n\{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n-B^y_{J_y,n}-B^z_{J_z,n}\}}{S_n}\right],
\mathcal L\left[\frac1{S_n}\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}
\{(\xi_{e,k}+\eta_{k,n})^2-(1+\eta_{k,n}^2)\}\right]
\right)\to0,
\]
where \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}B_{J_y,J_z,n}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}\), the spectrum is repeated twice,
\[
A_{J_y,J_z,n}^2=4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2,
\qquad
\eta_{k,n}=2^{-1/2}v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt n\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}.
\]
The same proxy and the normalized estimator are diffuse locally Gaussian:
\[
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L\left[\frac{n\{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n-B^y_{J_y,n}-B^z_{J_z,n}\}}{S_n}\right],
\mathcal N\!\left(0,\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}^2+nV_{L,n}}{S_n^2}\right)
\right)\to0.
\]
In particular, at equality all shifts and the linear projection vanish and
\[
\frac{n\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}}{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
If \(D_{J_y,J_z}\log n/m=o(1)\), the population kernel in the finite-\(n\) proxy may be replaced by the average observed kernel formed from \(\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\). Separately, at fixed unequal laws, if \(\widehat V_{L,n}/V_{L,n}\to_P1\), \(\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}/A_{J_y,J_z,n}\to\infty\), and the displayed bias and remainder are \(o(\sqrt{V_{L,n}/n})\), then
\[
\frac{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n}{\sqrt{\widehat V_{L,n}/n}}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
No fixed or subsequential non-Gaussian chaos is asserted in this growing-covariate-resolution regime.

V_{L,n}=n\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}),
\qquad
\widehat V_{L,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{1}{m-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\{\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})-\bar s_{a,e}\}^2.
\]
defs.def:whitened-spectral-array:
Let \(G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}\) be the Gram matrix in the anisotropic-projection definition and form the inverse-elliptic bilinear-form matrix
\[
H^{\mathrm{form}}_{J_y,J_z,n;\lambda\mu}
=\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}\Phi_\lambda(y,z)
\{\mathcal G_{n,z}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z)\}(y)\,dy\,dR_n(z).
\]
The Hessian in raw feature-moment coordinates is
\[
B_{J_y,J_z,n}=G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}H^{\mathrm{form}}_{J_y,J_z,n}G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}.
\]
Form \(\Gamma_{a,J_y,J_z,n}=\operatorname{Cov}_{P_{a,n}}\{\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,1,n})\}\), \(\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{0,J_y,J_z,n}+\Gamma_{1,J_y,J_z,n}\),
\[
K_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}B_{J_y,J_z,n}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2},
\qquad
\mathsf K_{J_y,J_z,n}=K_{J_y,J_z,n}\oplus K_{J_y,J_z,n}.
\]
Let \((\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n},v_{k,J_y,J_z,n})\) be the eigenpairs of the one-fold matrix, set
\[
\eta_{k,n}=v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt{n/2}\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n},
\qquad
A_{J_y,J_z,n}=\left\{4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\right\}^{1/2}.
\]

assumptions.ass:conditional-density-bounds: The conditional densities satisfy \(c\le q_{a,n}(y,z)\le C\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \((y,z)\in\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d\).
assumptions.ass:two-arm-sampling: For every \(n\), the observations \(W_{a,1,n},\ldots,W_{a,n,n}\) are i.i.d. from \(P_{a,n}\) within each \(a\in\mathcal A\), and the two arm samples are independent.

snapshot.stmt:
Assume \(L>1\), put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\), and fix \(d\ge1\). For every fixed \(0<\tau<\min\{s_y,s_z\}\), put \(a_\tau=\tau/(2\tau+d+1)\). There are constants \(c_1>0\) and \(C_{1,\tau}<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants and, for the upper constant, on \(\tau\), such that for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
c_1\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\le\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}\{E(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}
\]
\[
\le C_{1,\tau}\min\!\left\{
\rho^2,
\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2,
n^{-a_\tau}(\log n)^{a_\tau}
\right\}.
\]
When \(s_z\ge1\), a fourth candidate \(n^{-1/(d+2)}(\log n)^{1+1/(d+2)}\) may be inserted in the last minimum. Here
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}.
\]
The three nonzero upper candidates are attained, respectively, by the observable Gram-corrected estimator \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y^*,J_z^*,n}\), the median-aggregated SmoothCOT estimator \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{sm,med}}_{\tau,n}\), and, when \(s_z\ge1\), the median-aggregated direct-COT estimator \(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm{dir,med}}\); the first entry is attained by the zero estimator. The quadratic and zero-zone lower bounds hold on the explicit sign-paired family in the mixture-check lemma. In the zone \(\rho\gg n^{-1/2}\), extending \(q_{a,t}^{0}\) constantly in \(z\) and comparing amplitudes separated by order \(n^{-1/2}\) supplies the regular \(\rho n^{-1/2}\) lower bound.

The bracket is matched whenever
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2
=O\{\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}.
\]
Uniformly in \(0\le\rho\le1\), neither supplemental global envelope enlarges this matching region: \(a_\tau<\min\{1/2,4s_z/(4s_z+d)\}\), and, when \(s_z\ge1\), \(1/(d+2)<\min\{1/2,4s_z/(4s_z+d)\}\). In the matching region the intrinsic quadratic elbow is \(s_z=d/4\): when \(s_z>d/4\), \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\) and \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\) delimit zero, quadratic, mixed, and regular zones; when \(s_z\le d/4\), the quadratic term prevents a positive-variance root-\(n\) rate uniformly over the class. Outside the matching region, the sharpened two-sided bracket above is the conclusion and its tightness is not asserted.

defs.def:anisotropic-estimator:
Partition each arm into deterministic folds \(I_{a,1}\) and \(I_{a,2}\), each of size \(m=n/2\). On pilot fold \(3-e\), let \(\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be the empirical boundary-wavelet joint-density projection through \((\bar J_y,\bar J_z)\), and set \(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z)=\frac12\sum_{a=0}^1\int_0^1\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du\). With \(T(x)=\min\{2C,\max\{c/2,x\}\}\), define \(\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)=T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z))/\int T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(v))dv\), \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)/\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)\), and \(\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z))/\int_0^1T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z))du\). The event \(\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\) is \(c/2<\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}<2C\) and \(c/2<\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}<2C\) pointwise for both arms; clipping is inactive on this event, while normalization enforces exact conditional mass. The displayed operations keep every object defined on its complement. Put \(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}=(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}+\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)})/2\) and, on the oversampled zero-outcome-mean wavelet space through \(J_y^{\mathrm{op}}\), set
\[
\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}=
\left[P_{J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}\{-\partial_y(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)\partial_y)\}P_{J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}+\lambda_n I\right]^{-1}P_{J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)^{\top}\,dy\,\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz,
\]
\[
\widehat H_{\mathrm{form},J_y,J_z,n;\lambda\mu}^{(-e)}
=\int\Phi_\lambda(y,z)\{\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z)\}(y)\,dy\,\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz,
\]
and the raw-moment-coordinate Hessian
\[
\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
=\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}
\widehat H_{\mathrm{form},J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}.
\]
Let \(\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)=W_2^2(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy,\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy)\), let \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be its observable one-dimensional Kantorovich derivative in arm \(a\), and let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}=\int\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz\). The explicit first-order score is
\[
\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\frac12\{\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)-\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}\}+\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)-\int_0^1\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du.
\]
Set \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})-\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\), where \(\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\). The diagonal-free correction in raw moment coordinates is
\[
\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\frac{1}{m(m-1)}\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{i\ne j\in I_{a,e}}(X_{a,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{a,j}^{(-e)}-\frac{2}{m^2}\sum_{i\in I_{1,e}}\sum_{j\in I_{0,e}}(X_{1,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{0,j}^{(-e)}.
\]
Finally,
\[
\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}+\sum_{a=0}^1\frac1m\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})+\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n},
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}.
\]
defs.def:conditional-minimax-rate: For \(d\ge1\), define \(\mathfrak R_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}\), where \(r_{n,d}(s_z)=n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\). The zero-to-quadratic boundary is \(\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)}\), and the quadratic-to-linear boundary is \(\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/(2(4s_z+d))}\).
defs.def:model-class: \[\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}):\text{the declared sampling, common-marginal, density-bound, anisotropic-smoothness, and local-radius properties hold at indices }(n,d)\}.\]
defs.def:no-covariate-witness: For \(d=0\), set \(q_{a,t}^{0}(y)=1+(2a-1)t\cos(2\pi y)/2\); use the pairs \(t=0\) and \(t=c_0n^{-1/2}\) at equality, and \(t=t_0\) and \(t=t_0+c_0n^{-1/2}\) for a fixed sufficiently small \(t_0\ne0\).
defs.def:pilot-tuning-and-studentizer:
For \(d\ge1\), set \(\beta^{-1}=s_y^{-1}+ds_z^{-1}\), \(2^{\bar J_y}\asymp(n/\log n)^{\beta/(s_y(2\beta+1))}\), \(2^{\bar J_z}\asymp(n/\log n)^{\beta/(s_z(2\beta+1))}\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}=(\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\), and \(\lambda_n=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\). For each point-estimator outcome resolution, let \(J_y^{\mathrm{op}}\ge J_y\) be the smallest integer satisfying \(2^{-2J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\). Let \(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\) be the sum over \(a=0,1\) of the usual sample covariance of \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})\), \(i\in I_{a,3-e}\), and set
\[
\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}.
\]
If \(\bar s_{a,e}=m^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})\), define
\[
V_{L,n}=n\operatorname{Var}(\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}),
\qquad
\widehat V_{L,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_{a=0}^1\frac{1}{m-1}\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\{\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})-\bar s_{a,e}\}^2.
\]
defs.def:smoothcot-median-estimator:
Fix \(d\ge1\) and \(0<\tau<\min\{s_y,s_z\}\), and put \(a_\tau=\tau/(2\tau+d+1)\). Choose an odd integer \(K_n^{\mathrm{sm}}\asymp\log n\), with a sufficiently large fixed multiplier depending only on \((\tau,d)\), and set \(N_n^{\mathrm{sm}}=\lfloor n/K_n^{\mathrm{sm}}\rfloor\). Discard at most \(K_n^{\mathrm{sm}}-1\) observations per arm and split the remaining observations in each arm into \(K_n^{\mathrm{sm}}\) paired disjoint blocks of size \(N_n^{\mathrm{sm}}\).

On paired block \(\ell\), set
\[
J_{\tau,n}^{\mathrm{sm}}=
\left\lfloor\frac{\log_2 N_n^{\mathrm{sm}}}{2\tau+d+1}\right\rfloor
\]
and form the empirical tensor boundary-wavelet projection \(\widetilde p_{a,\ell,\tau}\) of the joint density on \([0,1]^{d+1}\) through this common isotropic resolution. Define the everywhere nonnegative normalized joint-density estimate
\[
\widehat p_{a,\ell,\tau}(y,z)=
\frac{\{\widetilde p_{a,\ell,\tau}(y,z)\}_+}
{\int\{\widetilde p_{a,\ell,\tau}(u,v)\}_+\,du\,dv},
\]
using the uniform density if the denominator is zero. Put \(\widehat r_{a,\ell,\tau}(z)=\int_0^1\widehat p_{a,\ell,\tau}(y,z)\,dy\) and \(\widehat r_{\ell,\tau}=(\widehat r_{0,\ell,\tau}+\widehat r_{1,\ell,\tau})/2\). Define
\[
\widehat q_{a,\ell,\tau}(y\mid z)=
\begin{cases}
\widehat p_{a,\ell,\tau}(y,z)/\widehat r_{a,\ell,\tau}(z),&\widehat r_{a,\ell,\tau}(z)>0,\\
1,&\widehat r_{a,\ell,\tau}(z)=0,
\end{cases}
\]
and reattach the pooled marginal:
\[
\widehat P_{a,\ell,\tau}^{\dagger}(dy,dz)
=\widehat q_{a,\ell,\tau}(y\mid z)\,dy\,\widehat r_{\ell,\tau}(z)\,dz.
\]
The block value and the final estimator are the explicit sample maps
\[
\widehat V_{\ell,\tau,n}^{\mathrm{sm}}
=\int W_2^2\!\left(\widehat P_{0,\ell,\tau}^{\dagger}(\cdot\mid z),
\widehat P_{1,\ell,\tau}^{\dagger}(\cdot\mid z)\right)
\widehat r_{\ell,\tau}(z)\,dz,
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{sm,med}}_{\tau,n}
=\operatorname{median}_{1\le\ell\le K_n^{\mathrm{sm}}}
\widehat V_{\ell,\tau,n}^{\mathrm{sm}}.
\]
All values lie in \([0,1]\), and every zero-denominator convention above is deterministic, so the estimator is defined on every sample.

assumptions.ass:anisotropic-conditional-smoothness: Each \(q_{a,n}\) belongs to the tensor anisotropic ball \(\mathcal C^{s_y,s_z}(\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d;L)\), with the \(z\)-condition omitted when \(d=0\).
assumptions.ass:conditional-density-bounds: The conditional densities satisfy \(c\le q_{a,n}(y,z)\le C\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \((y,z)\in\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d\).
assumptions.ass:holder-radius-interior: The H\"older radius satisfies \(L>1\), so the uniform density is an interior point of the declared H\"older balls.
assumptions.ass:shared-covariate-marginal: The \(\mathcal Z_d\)-marginal of \(P_{a,n}\) equals \(R_n\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).

assumptions.ass:covariate-density-bounds: For \(d\ge1\), the common marginal density satisfies \(c\le r_n(z)\le C\) for every \(z\in\mathcal Z_d\).

Put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\), \(e=\beta/(2\beta+1)\), \(b=4s_z/(4s_z+d)\), and \(\kappa=2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)\). For \(d\ge1\), uniform absorption of the H\"older-valid pilot remainder over the declared local-radius range means
\[
\sup_{0\le\rho\le1}
\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho^{a_y\kappa}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2}
{\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-b}}=O(1).
\]
This absorption holds, with strict exponent inequalities forced by the logarithmic pilot factor, if and only if
\[
s_z>\frac{3d}{4}
\quad\text{and}\quad
s_y>
\frac{s_z\!\left[11d+4s_z+\sqrt{(4s_z-d)(100s_z+23d)}\right]}
{2(4s_z-3d)(2s_z+d)}.
\]
Equivalently, the second condition is
\[
(4s_z-3d)(2s_z+d)s_y^2-s_z(11d+4s_z)s_y-12s_z^2>0.
\]
Consequently, throughout exactly this region the Gram-corrected local upper bound in \(\mathrm{thm{:}conditional\text{-}minimax\text{-}frontier}\) attains the intrinsic frontier uniformly in \(0\le\rho\le1\). Thus \(s_z=d/4\) is the intrinsic minimax elbow, whereas uniform sharpness of the present observable pilot construction begins only beyond \(s_z=3d/4\) and the displayed outcome-smoothness threshold.

There are two supplemental global estimators. First, for every fixed \(0<\tau<\min\{s_y,s_z\}\), put \(a_\tau=\tau/(2\tau+d+1)\) and use the explicit blockwise aligned wavelet construction in \(\mathrm{def{:}smoothcot\text{-}median\text{-}estimator}\). Its median satisfies, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\left\{E(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{sm,med}}_{\tau,n}-\theta_n)^2\right\}^{1/2}
\lesssim_\tau n^{-a_\tau}(\log n)^{a_\tau}.
\]
Second, when \(s_z\ge1\), choose an odd \(K_n\asymp\log n\), split each arm into \(K_n\) disjoint blocks of size \(N_n=\lfloor n/K_n\rfloor\), and on every block use covariate cells of side \(N_n^{-1/(d+2)}\). Project each covariate to its cell center; at each occupied center form the empirical conditional outcome law; optimally couple the two projected empirical covariate marginals in Euclidean distance; integrate the squared Wasserstein distance between paired empirical conditional outcome laws; and take the median of the block values. Then
\[
\left\{E(\widehat\theta_n^{\mathrm{dir,med}}-\theta_n)^2\right\}^{1/2}
\lesssim n^{-1/(d+2)}(\log n)^{1+1/(d+2)}.
\]
Accordingly, the upper side of the minimax bracket is the minimum of \(\rho^2\), the theorem's Gram-corrected pilot envelope, and the SmoothCOT envelope for every fixed admissible \(\tau\), with the direct-COT envelope inserted when \(s_z\ge1\). These additions sharpen an otherwise pilot-dominated upper bracket but do not enlarge the exact uniform matching region: \(a_\tau<\min\{b,1/2\}\), and, for \(s_z\ge1\), \(1/(d+2)<\min\{b,1/2\}\). Outside the displayed pilot-feasibility region the sharpened bracket is the conclusion, and equality of its two sides is not asserted.

Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\), there are fixed constants \(0<c_H<C_H<\infty\) and \(0<c_\Gamma<C_\Gamma<\infty\) such that, if \(g=\sum_{(j_y,k_y,\gamma)\in\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}\psi^y_{j_y,k_y}\psi^z_\gamma\), then
\[
c_H\sum_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}2^{-2j_y}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}^2
\le\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}g(y,z)\{\mathcal G_{n,z}g(\cdot,z)\}(y)dydR_n(z)
\le C_H\sum_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}2^{-2j_y}x_{j_y,k_y,\gamma}^2,
\]
and \(c_\Gamma I\preceq\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}\preceq C_\Gamma I\). Consequently there are fixed \(0<\underline c<\overline C<\infty\) such that, for every \(u>0\),
\[
\left|\left\{(j_y,k_y,\gamma)\in\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}:\underline c\,2^{-2j_y}\ge u\right\}\right|
\le N_{J_y,J_z,n}(u)
\le
\left|\left\{(j_y,k_y,\gamma)\in\Lambda_{J_y,J_z}^{(d)}:\overline C\,2^{-2j_y}\ge u\right\}\right|.
\]
Writing \(j_0\) for the fixed coarsest retained outcome level, throughout the nonempty range \(\overline C2^{-2J_y}\le u\le\underline c2^{-2j_0}\),
\[
N_{J_y,J_z,n}(u)\asymp\min\{D_{J_y,J_z},2^{dJ_z}u^{-1/2}\},
\qquad
\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}\asymp\min\{1,(2^{dJ_z}/k)^2\},\quad 1\le k\le D_{J_y,J_z}.
\]
Consequently, for \(d\ge1\),
\[
\|K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\asymp1,
\qquad \|K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\asymp2^{dJ_z},
\qquad
\frac{\max_k|\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}|}{\{\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\}^{1/2}}
\lesssim2^{-dJ_z/2}.
\]
The same quadratic-form comparison and anisotropic approximation give \(|B^y_{J_y,n}|\lesssim2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}\) and \(|B^z_{J_z,n}|\lesssim2^{-2s_zJ_z}\). When \(d=0\), the Hilbert--Schmidt norm remains bounded above and away from zero as \(J_y\to\infty\).

defs.def:anisotropic-projection:
Let
\[
G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}=\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}
\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)^{\top}\,dy\,dR_n(z).
\]
For \(d\ge1\), define the \(L^2(dy\,dR_n)\)-orthogonal projection by
\[
\Pi_{J_y,J_z}h
=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}^{\top}G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}
\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)h(y,z)\,dy\,dR_n(z).
\]
For \(d=0\), \(G_{R,J_y,0,n}=I\) and the same formula retains only the outcome-wavelet sum through \(J_y\).
defs.def:model-class: \[\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}):\text{the declared sampling, common-marginal, density-bound, anisotropic-smoothness, and local-radius properties hold at indices }(n,d)\}.\]
defs.def:whitened-spectral-array:
Let \(G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}\) be the Gram matrix in the anisotropic-projection definition and form the inverse-elliptic bilinear-form matrix
\[
H^{\mathrm{form}}_{J_y,J_z,n;\lambda\mu}
=\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}\Phi_\lambda(y,z)
\{\mathcal G_{n,z}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z)\}(y)\,dy\,dR_n(z).
\]
The Hessian in raw feature-moment coordinates is
\[
B_{J_y,J_z,n}=G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}H^{\mathrm{form}}_{J_y,J_z,n}G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}.
\]
Form \(\Gamma_{a,J_y,J_z,n}=\operatorname{Cov}_{P_{a,n}}\{\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,1,n})\}\), \(\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{0,J_y,J_z,n}+\Gamma_{1,J_y,J_z,n}\),
\[
K_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}B_{J_y,J_z,n}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2},
\qquad
\mathsf K_{J_y,J_z,n}=K_{J_y,J_z,n}\oplus K_{J_y,J_z,n}.
\]
Let \((\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n},v_{k,J_y,J_z,n})\) be the eigenpairs of the one-fold matrix, set
\[
\eta_{k,n}=v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt{n/2}\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n},
\qquad
A_{J_y,J_z,n}=\left\{4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\right\}^{1/2}.
\]

assumptions.ass:anisotropic-conditional-smoothness: Each \(q_{a,n}\) belongs to the tensor anisotropic ball \(\mathcal C^{s_y,s_z}(\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d;L)\), with the \(z\)-condition omitted when \(d=0\).

assumptions.ass:covariate-density-bounds: For \(d\ge1\), the common marginal density satisfies \(c\le r_n(z)\le C\) for every \(z\in\mathcal Z_d\).
assumptions.ass:wavelet-regularity: The bases \(\Psi_y\) and \(\Psi_z\) are compactly supported boundary wavelets with regularities strictly greater than \(s_y+1\) and \(s_z\), respectively.
assumptions.ass:two-arm-sampling: For every \(n\), the observations \(W_{a,1,n},\ldots,W_{a,n,n}\) are i.i.d. from \(P_{a,n}\) within each \(a\in\mathcal A\), and the two arm samples are independent.

Let \(d\ge1\) and put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\). For the opposite-fold estimator and the declared pilot resolutions, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\max_e\left[\|\widehat r_n^{(-e)}-r_n\|_\infty+\max_a\|\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}-q_{a,n}\|_\infty\right]=O_P(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}),
\qquad
P\left(\bigcap_{e=1}^2\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\right)\to1.
\]
The clipping is inactive on that event, and conditional normalization is exact everywhere. The fixed density bounds imply
\[
\frac{c}{4C}I\preceq G_{R,J_y,J_z,n},\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\preceq\frac{4C}{c}I
\]
for every fold and every realization. Moreover,
\[
\max_e\left[
\|\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}-G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-B_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\right]
=O_P(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{a_y}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}+\lambda_n).
\]
The plug-in, Gram, ridge, and operator contribution to the second-order expansion is
\[
O_P\!\left\{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+
\rho_n^{\,2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2\right\}
+o_P(1)\left\{\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}n\right\}.
\]
Hence it is negligible relative to the displayed expansion scale whenever
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho_n^{\,2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2
=o\!\left(\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}n+2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}\right).
\]
If additionally \(D_{J_y,J_z}\log n/m=o(1)\), then
\[
\max_e\|\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),
\qquad
\max_e\|\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),
\]
and \(\max_e\|\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}-K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}=o_P(\|K_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{\mathrm{HS}})\). This extra covariance condition is required only when the population triangular proxy is replaced by its observed spectral plug-in, not for the point estimator.

defs.def:anisotropic-estimator:
Partition each arm into deterministic folds \(I_{a,1}\) and \(I_{a,2}\), each of size \(m=n/2\). On pilot fold \(3-e\), let \(\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be the empirical boundary-wavelet joint-density projection through \((\bar J_y,\bar J_z)\), and set \(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z)=\frac12\sum_{a=0}^1\int_0^1\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du\). With \(T(x)=\min\{2C,\max\{c/2,x\}\}\), define \(\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)=T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(z))/\int T(\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}(v))dv\), \(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\widetilde p_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)/\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)\), and \(\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z))/\int_0^1T(\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z))du\). The event \(\mathcal E_n^{(-e)}\) is \(c/2<\widetilde r_n^{(-e)}<2C\) and \(c/2<\check q_{a,n}^{(-e)}<2C\) pointwise for both arms; clipping is inactive on this event, while normalization enforces exact conditional mass. The displayed operations keep every object defined on its complement. Put \(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}=(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}+\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)})/2\) and, on the oversampled zero-outcome-mean wavelet space through \(J_y^{\mathrm{op}}\), set
\[
\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}=
\left[P_{J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}\{-\partial_y(\widehat{\bar q}_n^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)\partial_y)\}P_{J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}+\lambda_n I\right]^{-1}P_{J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)^{\top}\,dy\,\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz,
\]
\[
\widehat H_{\mathrm{form},J_y,J_z,n;\lambda\mu}^{(-e)}
=\int\Phi_\lambda(y,z)\{\widehat{\mathcal G}_{n,z}^{(-e)}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z)\}(y)\,dy\,\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz,
\]
and the raw-moment-coordinate Hessian
\[
\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
=\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}
\widehat H_{\mathrm{form},J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}
\{\widehat G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\}^{-1}.
\]
Let \(\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)=W_2^2(\widehat q_{0,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy,\widehat q_{1,n}^{(-e)}(\cdot,z)dy)\), let \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}\) be its observable one-dimensional Kantorovich derivative in arm \(a\), and let \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}=\int\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)\widehat r_n^{(-e)}(z)dz\). The explicit first-order score is
\[
\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)=\frac12\{\widehat f_n^{(-e)}(z)-\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}\}+\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(y,z)-\int_0^1\widehat\ell_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}(u,z)du.
\]
Set \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})-\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\), where \(\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\). The diagonal-free correction in raw moment coordinates is
\[
\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\frac{1}{m(m-1)}\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{i\ne j\in I_{a,e}}(X_{a,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{a,j}^{(-e)}-\frac{2}{m^2}\sum_{i\in I_{1,e}}\sum_{j\in I_{0,e}}(X_{1,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{0,j}^{(-e)}.
\]
Finally,
\[
\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}+\sum_{a=0}^1\frac1m\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})+\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n},
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}.
\]

Let \(d\ge1\), put \(a_y=\min\{s_y,1\}\), let \(J_y,J_z\to\infty\), let \(D_{J_y,J_z}=o(n^2)\), and use the observable anisotropic estimator with the declared pilot tuning and studentizer. If
\[

\[
\frac{\rho_n}{\sqrt n}+r_{n,d}(s_z)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^{2+a_y}+\rho_n^{2a_y/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2,
\]

Set \(X_{a,i}^{(-e)}=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})-\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\), where \(\widehat\mu_{a,J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=\int\Phi_{J_y,J_z}\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}\widehat r_n^{(-e)}\). The diagonal-free correction in raw moment coordinates is
\[
\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\frac{1}{m(m-1)}\sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{i\ne j\in I_{a,e}}(X_{a,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{a,j}^{(-e)}-\frac{2}{m^2}\sum_{i\in I_{1,e}}\sum_{j\in I_{0,e}}(X_{1,i}^{(-e)})^\top\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}X_{0,j}^{(-e)}.
\]
Finally,
\[
\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{plug}}^{(-e)}+\sum_{a=0}^1\frac1m\sum_{i\in I_{a,e}}\widehat s_{a,n}^{(-e)}(W_{a,i,n})+\widehat U_{e,J_y,J_z,n},
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}=\frac12\sum_{e=1}^2\widehat\theta_{e,J_y,J_z,n}.
\]
defs.def:anisotropic-projection:
Let
\[
G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}=\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}
\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)^{\top}\,dy\,dR_n(z).
\]
For \(d\ge1\), define the \(L^2(dy\,dR_n)\)-orthogonal projection by
\[
\Pi_{J_y,J_z}h
=\Phi_{J_y,J_z}^{\top}G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}
\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(y,z)h(y,z)\,dy\,dR_n(z).
\]
For \(d=0\), \(G_{R,J_y,0,n}=I\) and the same formula retains only the outcome-wavelet sum through \(J_y\).

For \(d\ge1\), set \(\beta^{-1}=s_y^{-1}+ds_z^{-1}\), \(2^{\bar J_y}\asymp(n/\log n)^{\beta/(s_y(2\beta+1))}\), \(2^{\bar J_z}\asymp(n/\log n)^{\beta/(s_z(2\beta+1))}\), \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}=(\log n/n)^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}\), and \(\lambda_n=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\). For each point-estimator outcome resolution, let \(J_y^{\mathrm{op}}\ge J_y\) be the smallest integer satisfying \(2^{-2J_y^{\mathrm{op}}}\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}\). Let \(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\) be the sum over \(a=0,1\) of the usual sample covariance of \(\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,i,n})\), \(i\in I_{a,3-e}\), and set
\[
\widehat K_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}=(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}(\widehat\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)})^{1/2}.
\]

\[

\qquad

defs.def:whitened-spectral-array:
Let \(G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}\) be the Gram matrix in the anisotropic-projection definition and form the inverse-elliptic bilinear-form matrix
\[
H^{\mathrm{form}}_{J_y,J_z,n;\lambda\mu}
=\int_{\mathcal Z_d}\int_{\mathcal Y}\Phi_\lambda(y,z)
\{\mathcal G_{n,z}\Phi_\mu(\cdot,z)\}(y)\,dy\,dR_n(z).
\]
The Hessian in raw feature-moment coordinates is
\[
B_{J_y,J_z,n}=G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}H^{\mathrm{form}}_{J_y,J_z,n}G_{R,J_y,J_z,n}^{-1}.
\]
Form \(\Gamma_{a,J_y,J_z,n}=\operatorname{Cov}_{P_{a,n}}\{\Phi_{J_y,J_z}(W_{a,1,n})\}\), \(\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{0,J_y,J_z,n}+\Gamma_{1,J_y,J_z,n}\),
\[
K_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}B_{J_y,J_z,n}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2},
\qquad
\mathsf K_{J_y,J_z,n}=K_{J_y,J_z,n}\oplus K_{J_y,J_z,n}.
\]
Let \((\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n},v_{k,J_y,J_z,n})\) be the eigenpairs of the one-fold matrix, set
\[

\qquad
A_{J_y,J_z,n}=\left\{4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2\right\}^{1/2}.
\]

assumptions.ass:conditional-density-bounds: The conditional densities satisfy \(c\le q_{a,n}(y,z)\le C\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and \((y,z)\in\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Z_d\).
assumptions.ass:covariate-density-bounds: For \(d\ge1\), the common marginal density satisfies \(c\le r_n(z)\le C\) for every \(z\in\mathcal Z_d\).
assumptions.ass:shared-covariate-marginal: The \(\mathcal Z_d\)-marginal of \(P_{a,n}\) equals \(R_n\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).
assumptions.ass:two-arm-sampling: For every \(n\), the observations \(W_{a,1,n},\ldots,W_{a,n,n}\) are i.i.d. from \(P_{a,n}\) within each \(a\in\mathcal A\), and the two arm samples are independent.
assumptions.ass:wavelet-regularity: The bases \(\Psi_y\) and \(\Psi_z\) are compactly supported boundary wavelets with regularities strictly greater than \(s_y+1\) and \(s_z\), respectively.

Under the uniform second-order expansion, suppose additionally that \(\|\Delta_n\|_\infty\to0\) and
\[
2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}=O(S_n/n),
\qquad
S_n=A_{J_y,J_z,n}+\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}.
\]
Then the finite-\(n\) Gaussian-quadratic proxy based on the corrected raw-moment kernel satisfies
\[
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L\left[\frac{n\{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n-B^y_{J_y,n}-B^z_{J_z,n}\}}{S_n}\right],
\mathcal L\left[\frac1{S_n}\sum_{e=1}^2\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}
\{(\xi_{e,k}+\eta_{k,n})^2-(1+\eta_{k,n}^2)\}\right]
\right)\to0,
\]
where \(K_{J_y,J_z,n}=\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}B_{J_y,J_z,n}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{1/2}\), the spectrum is repeated twice,
\[
A_{J_y,J_z,n}^2=4\sum_k\nu_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^2,
\qquad
\eta_{k,n}=2^{-1/2}v_{k,J_y,J_z,n}^{\top}\Gamma_{J_y,J_z,n}^{-1/2}\sqrt n\,\delta_{J_y,J_z,n}.
\]
The same proxy and the normalized estimator are diffuse locally Gaussian:
\[
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L\left[\frac{n\{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n-B^y_{J_y,n}-B^z_{J_z,n}\}}{S_n}\right],
\mathcal N\!\left(0,\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}^2+nV_{L,n}}{S_n^2}\right)
\right)\to0.
\]
In particular, at equality all shifts and the linear projection vanish and
\[
\frac{n\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}}{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
If \(D_{J_y,J_z}\log n/m=o(1)\), the population kernel in the finite-\(n\) proxy may be replaced by the average observed kernel formed from \(\widehat B_{J_y,J_z,n}^{(-e)}\). Separately, at fixed unequal laws, if \(\widehat V_{L,n}/V_{L,n}\to_P1\), \(\sqrt{nV_{L,n}}/A_{J_y,J_z,n}\to\infty\), and the displayed bias and remainder are \(o(\sqrt{V_{L,n}/n})\), then
\[
\frac{\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n}{\sqrt{\widehat V_{L,n}/n}}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
No fixed or subsequential non-Gaussian chaos is asserted in this growing-covariate-resolution regime.
